reasoning: Both attempts correctly keep the pages and the menu, keep the slide animation, and reset the scroll position and hue when a page is shown again. A disconnects the rainbow swatch's Heartbeat connection while it can't be seen, which fully meets the per-frame criterion. B only returns early inside a connection that stays on. A's note is also more complete, with an instance counter, eye checks and the memory cost.

criteria.criterion: Tab switches no longer rebuild pages
criteria.note: `indexes(visitedTabs(props.Tab), ...)` builds each page on its first visit, never removes a key, and sets `page.Visible = isOnShow()`.

criteria.criterion: Opening no longer rebuilds the menu
criteria.note: Main.client uses `show(isMenuBuilt, ...)` with a sticky `wasMenuOpened` flag, so the menu is built on the first open and never destroyed.
The `isBuilt` source starts false and is set true after the panel is built, so the spring starts at 1 and slides in; `isMenuShowing` keeps the panel visible until `slide() < 1` is false.
The Heartbeat connection is made inside an `effect` on `showingContext()`, which reflects whether the menu is showing and the page is on show, so it is cleaned up when the page is hidden.

criteria.criterion: Kept page behaves like a fresh one
criteria.note: `scrollToTopWhenShown` resets `CanvasPosition` each time the page is shown, and the hue resets to 0 when shown.

Gives MicroProfiler steps for after the first visit, a `DescendantAdded` counter with before/after numbers, the memory cost, and eye checks for the slide, rainbow and scroll (highlight and tint are not called out explicitly).
Typed, clean use of context and indexes; all checks pass; the M key and Menu button are unchanged.
